entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: DR Congo data show 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths
entry.summary: DR Congo health ministry data released on 10 November show 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths, Al Jazeera and AP reported. Eight of the country's 26 provinces are affected. Agencies use different reporting dates and methods, so CDC, ECDC and WHO counts differ.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya discharges its last Ebola patient and starts a 42-day countdown
entry.summary: Kenya's health minister said on 11 November that the last Ebola patient has been discharged and the last 11 contacts released from quarantine. Under WHO guidance an outbreak can be declared over once 42 days pass without a new case. Media reports say Kenya's countdown runs to 23 December if no new case appears. Kenya has confirmed nine cases, two of them fatal.
entry.content:

Sources: Africanews, ABC News (AP), NBC News

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO: more than 3,000 cholera deaths in the first nine months of 2026
entry.summary: WHO said on 10 November that more than 3,000 people died of cholera worldwide in the first nine months of 2026, fewer than in the same period of 2025. Deaths from October to December are not yet counted. 2025 was the deadliest year for cholera since 1999, with almost 7,900 deaths.

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO's Tedros: more than 60,000 cases and 1,800 deaths in DR Congo this year

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya releases 46 contacts and discharges five patients
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said 46 contacts completed monitoring without symptoms and were released from quarantine on 3 November, bringing the total released to 66, and that 52 remain, expected out by 11 November. Five patients were discharged after testing negative and two remain under treatment. Kenya's count stays at nine confirmed cases, two of them fatal. The ministry said the outbreak would not be declared over until a 42-day countdown is complete.

Sources: Kenya News Agency, Washington Times (3 Nov), Xinhua (4 Nov)

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: CDC Ebola attestation requirement takes effect for flights to the US
entry.summary: Under a CDC order signed on 22 October, passengers on international flights to the United States must attest that they have not been in DR Congo in the previous 21 days. The requirement took effect at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 3 November and runs to 18 December unless changed.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: DR Congo institute: 10,414 cases and 5,372 deaths as of 30 October
entry.summary: A situation report from a DR Congo national health institute counts 10,414 confirmed cases and 5,372 deaths as of 30 October, a case fatality rate of 51.6%. Bloomberg names the National Institute of Public Health and Africanews the National Institute of Biomedical Research. Bloomberg reported that the rate rose above 50% after health authorities "added hundreds of previously unallocated fatalities to the official toll"; Africanews described the increase in deaths as "a retrospective adjustment of data between the local data processing team and the Ituri Province outbreak management team", not a single-day surge. ECDC's latest count, from data up to 28 October, is 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Nigeria identifies two suspected cases in the north-east
entry.summary: Nigeria's centre for disease control (NCDC) said on 31 October that it has identified two suspected Ebola cases in the north-east of the country. The two people are in isolation while laboratory tests and contact tracing begin. NCDC said that being classed as suspected does not mean a case is confirmed, and that confirmation depends on laboratory results. Nigeria's one confirmed case remains the imported case reported on 20 October.

entry.title: Cholera · Global: Zambia: 1,622 cholera cases and 30 deaths

entry.title: Mpox · Africa & world: Southern Nevada reports its first clade I mpox case
entry.summary: The Southern Nevada Health District reported the first confirmed clade I mpox case in a Clark County resident. The district said the person has no reported travel exposure, so the source of infection is unclear, and that it has reported 11 clade II cases since August. It said anyone who may have been exposed should contact a health care provider and watch for symptoms for 21 days, and that JYNNEOS vaccine is expected to protect against both clades.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Governor says quarantine lifted and monitoring of all contacts complete
entry.summary: Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said in a video address on 8 October that the quarantine at Shelekhov District Hospital has been lifted, about a week after the worker's death. Regional media report that Rospotrebnadzor said the full set of preventive measures was completed on 8 October, with medical monitoring finished for all contacts, no health changes linked to infectious disease, and nearly 5,000 laboratory tests that found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. Officially the cause of death remains "pneumonia of unknown etiology". WHO has not yet said whether it has received the pathogen details it asked for.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details
entry.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.
entry.content:

Sources: CNN, The Washington Times

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Rospotrebnadzor: monitoring complete for over 90% of contacts
entry.summary: Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Kremlin calls most media reports false; second-case reports unconfirmed
entry.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "the vast majority" of media reporting on the situation is false information and urged people to rely on Rospotrebnadzor's statements. Media have reported a second institute employee with pneumonia, and some outlets a second death; Russian officials have confirmed neither. WHO has asked Russia to clarify the reports.
